definitions.meaning: to land is to descend to the ground, as an aircraft does
a blow here is a humiliating setback or fall in status

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike someone successfully.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft landing descends from the sky; a setback that lowers someone's standing is the same phrase as a noun.

clue.text: Mrs Wagner is turning in her sleep

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a coma is a deep, unnatural sleep

indicators.note: turning means the word is is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The composer's wife tosses and turns at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses 'is' before 'in' places it. Cosima, daughter of Liszt, was the second wife of the composer Richard Wagner.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosima, daughter of Liszt, married Richard Wagner and later ran the Bayreuth festival.

definitions.meaning: covered in the red spots of a well-known childhood illness

explanation.definitionFit: Measles marks the skin with spots, and the same adjective is slang for contemptibly mean or meagre.

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so these letters are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe of game bird and minced meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mince' looks like part of a dish but it is the anagram signal for GROUSE plus AND. 'Hairy' is informal for frightening or perilous.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy is slang for risky or alarming, as in a hairy moment on the road.

clue.text: Gate attendant may get the strikers out

definitions.meaning: a wicket is a small gate, and its keeper looks after it
in cricket the fielder behind the stumps can dismiss batsmen by catching or stumping

explanation.definitionFit: A wicket is also a small gate, so its guardian fits; in cricket the gloved fielder behind the stumps dismisses batsmen.

clue.text: Short-sighted? Gosh, the eye has lost its focus!

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh

indicators.note: losing its focus means the central letter of the word for an eye is dropped

parts.note: optic is a literary or humorous word for an eye

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that their vision has gone blurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost its focus' drops the central letter of the eye-word; 'Gosh' and 'My!' are both mild exclamations of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is the medical name for being unable to see distant things clearly.

definitions.meaning: a phrase from Shakespeare for one's green, inexperienced early years, and a popular 1950s musical

explanation.definitionFit: A lad is a young person, and salad days are the green years of early life.

definitions.meaning: a tender is a formal offer, as for a contract
a motion is a suggestion put before a meeting

explanation.definitionFit: A formal offer and a motion put to a meeting are both things put forward for acceptance.

parts.note: draughts reads as cold air currents that something keeps in check, but it is also the board game, which Americans call by a different name

explanation.definitionFit: The board game played with round pieces on a chequered board goes by this name in American English.

clue.text: Narrow connecting part on pen perhaps has curved shape

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits before the second

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a neck is a narrow part joining two wider ones, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: Describing a fountain pen whose slim joint bends in a curve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' suggests a writing instrument, but it is a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe or tap bent into an S-shape is named after the long curving neck of the bird.

clue.text: Word of warning about 27 place in uproar

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other

parts.note: golfers shout fore to warn those in the path of the ball
Ur was a city of the Chaldeans, the answer to 27 across

explanation.surface: A warning shouted in some unspecified place of commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; the cross-reference points to the Chaldeans, whose city was Ur of the Chaldees in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A furore is a public outburst of anger or excitement, a commotion.

parts.note: French is the language of France
Polish is the language of Poland

explanation.surface: A claim to excel in a pair of foreign tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shine' is the gloss made by this furniture finish, shellac rubbed in to a high gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: This shellac finish gives wooden furniture a deep glossy lustre.

clue.text: General confession by compiler in a muddle

parts.note: the setter owning up says it's me
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

explanation.surface: An army commander admits something to the setter while confused.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse of the clue's order: ME, then General Robert E. Lee of the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused scrum or brawl, a disordered jumble of people.

definitions.meaning: a defensive bank or rampart of soil
read literally, labour done on soil, the sort a digger does

explanation.definitionFit: A rampart of piled soil is a defensive structure, and literally it is labour on soil done by digging.

clue.text: Hardly a safe seat -occupant apt to keep moving

definitions.text: Hardly a safe seat -occupant apt to keep moving

parts.words: Hardly a safe seat -occupant apt to keep moving
parts.note: sounds like a marginal parliamentary constituency whose member may lose it, but describes a piece of furniture that sways to and fro under the sitter

explanation.definitionFit: A seat on curved runners sways back and forth, keeping whoever sits in it in motion.

parts.note: close weather is heavy, humid and oppressive
a call is a summons

explanation.surface: Getting away from a heavy-handed legal demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oppressive' refers to the weather: close means muggy and stifling.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss with danger is something you escaped only just.

parts.note: reads like an electricity grid sharing out current, but means a form of government in which political power is held equally by all

explanation.definitionFit: This rare term means government in which every citizen holds an equal share of political power.

parts.note: sounds like a fuss holding up a flight, but describes a hinged panel raised on an aircraft to slow it

explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel on an aircraft is raised into the airflow to slow it down.

parts.note: a spinster is an unmarried woman
a hood is a hoodlum, a gangster

explanation.surface: A woman crook locked up alone in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solitary confinement' is a playful definition: the unmarried state keeps a woman single, on her own.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being an unmarried woman is jokingly pictured as being kept on one's own.

clue.text: Sought the best Rover scout section

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from the words, so the letters sit inside best Rover

explanation.surface: A senior scout who aimed high, in the scouting movement's older branch.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover Scouts were the senior branch of the Scout movement; here 'section' signals letters taken from inside 'best Rover'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean tried hard to reach or obtain something.

clue.text: Note on fabric in coloured chalk

parts.note: C is a musical note
rayon is a synthetic fabric

explanation.surface: A remark about a cloth, written in chalk.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick of pigmented wax or chalk used for drawing, especially by children.

clue.text: "The Spanish Gentleman's" plot has an extraordinary role

definitions.note: the apostrophe s stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a cabal is a secret plot or faction

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters of role are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A play's hero has a remarkable part in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' signals the anagram; 'plot' means a conspiracy, not a storyline, and the possessive 's is really 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spain the word denotes a gentleman or knight, originally a horseman.

clue.text: A lord retaining the appearance of a landed proprietor

indicators.note: retaining means the abbreviation holds the other word within it

parts.note: an air is a look or manner, an appearance

explanation.surface: A nobleman keeping up the look of a rich landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the owner of a large estate is given this title.

clue.text: Put one's name down for record

definitions.meaning: sign up, as for a race or competition
write in, as in a ledger or register

explanation.definitionFit: Signing up for a competition and writing an item into a register are both this verb.

clue.text: A Spaniard, say, adopts one kind of dancing

indicators.note: adopts means the word takes in another letter

parts.note: dago is an old, offensive slang term for a Spaniard or other southern European
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man from Spain takes up a style of dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopts' puts I inside DAGO, a dated slur for a Spaniard, after A. In ballet the slow, sustained part is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet the slow section of sustained, graceful movements is named after the musical tempo marking.

indicators.note: first means the bird comes at the front

parts.note: mina is a variant spelling of mynah, an Asian starling
blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a Tory

explanation.surface: A bluebird gives the first sign of danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' is a Conservative, from the party's colour; Tory is the everyday British name for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Menacing and threatening, giving notice of harm to come.

definitions.meaning: produces, as a tree bears fruit
harvests, the produce of the land

explanation.definitionFit: A field produces a harvest, and the harvest it gives is the same word as a noun.

indicators.note: free suggests letters released from their order and set loose

explanation.surface: A freelance worker spoke an ancient language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freelance' is one printed word that splits: its front part 'Free' is the anagram signal and the rest is fodder, joined by 'had'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Semitic tongue of the people of southern Babylonia, an Aramaic form.
